intent: A World Stroke Day Short that stays a map story: three giants, one answer, the scale shown as counters that keep climbing, then the FAST card as the thing you actually take away.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country records the MOST stroke deaths every year?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country records the most stroke deaths every year?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: China. Over 2 million stroke deaths every year, about 1 in 3 of the whole world's total.

lines.direction: fly across the Pacific so both giants share the frame; the US lights up on 'States', its counter climbs to 165,000 and stops on 'thousand'; on 'sixteen' China pulses hard
lines.text: The United States loses about 165,000 a year. China's toll is 16 times that.

lines.direction: pull out to the whole stage; the world counter runs to 7,300,000 and the globe sticker drops on 'Earth'
lines.text: Worldwide, stroke kills more than 7 million people every single year, the third most common cause of death on Earth.

lines.direction: back onto China; the World Stroke Day card lands on 'Day', the brain sticker on 'FAST', the FAST card on 'face', the phone sticker on 'time'
lines.text: World Stroke Day is October 29. Remember FAST: face, arm, speech, and time to call for help.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
